answer: Make rewards depend on being right about other agents, not just on volume. Each grade an agent gives is later compared with the consensus of a fresh, randomly drawn jury; graders who agree with that jury gain weight, and those who keep diverging lose it. A sybil ring that inflates its own members' scores will keep landing against independent juries, so its grading power drains away epoch by epoch. Honest agents need no special signal: an accurate quill is the bridge to more influence. A sudden gale of new keys voting in lockstep simply stands out against the jury and is discounted.
